setlist.title: Stuck Inside Of Mobile With The Memphis Blues Again

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Never Trust A Woman** (2 reviews): Named as a first-set highlight, alongside Stagger Lee; Called a spicy standout, with Brent sounding fine despite apparently feeling poorly [17][19]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Judged slinky but middling and slight, after days in the city [19]
- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 review): Extended to almost five minutes, simple and spiffy [19]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Described as one of the most heartfelt versions ever, moving the reviewer to tears [18]
- **Throwing Stones** (1 review): Weir's microphone cut out, so the audience had to sing the rest of the verse [17]
- Reviewer praises a version with passion and harmonies, but the song isn't identified [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-09-18.164210.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 140 min [1]
- **gd1988-09-18.163947.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 19 songs; 140 min [2]
- **gd1988-09-18.140946.OTS.Schoeps.PCM.Mattes.Miller.Noel.t-flac.1644**: source not stated; 19 songs; 147 min [3]
- **gd88-09-18.sbd.eD.12746.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 134 min; rated 3.62/5 by 13 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard sounds really good, listened to on a laptop at work [16]
- **gd1988-09-18.nak300.damico.90920.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 134 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [12]. Said about its sound: Audience recording judged to sound much better than the soundboard source; Reviewer agrees the soundboard lacks punch and prefers the audience recording [23][24]

## Around the show

- A very long break before set two led the crowd to start a Not Fade Away chant [17]
- Reviewer mentions an enthusiastic crowd and Weir wearing tight jean shorts [18]
- Fourth night of a nine-night Madison Square Garden residency [3]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-09-18.164210.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac1644**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [1]
- **gd1988-09-18.163947.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  March 12, 2023; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [2]
- **gd1988-09-18.140946.OTS.Schoeps.PCM.Mattes.Miller.Noel.t-flac.1644**: taped by Don Crandall & Chris Huron; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel and Ted Mattes; source: Recording info: Schoeps CMC3/MK4 > PCM (Nakamichi DMP-100) (Sony ESX-HiFi/L-750 Beta tape); Transfer info: Sony SL-10 > Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer Ultramatch… [3]. Also: Schoeps-based recording with small digital pops cleaned up throughout the show [3]
- **gd88-09-18.sbd.eD.12746.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>MC>C?>DAT>CDR [4]. Also: Soundboard transferred through MC and DAT to CDR via Jools, then seeded to etree by eD [4]
- **gd1988-09-18.nak300.damico.90920.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Joe D'Amico; transferred by Joe D'Amico; source: nak 300 mics w/ cp4 shotguns > sony d-5 D [12]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Madison Square Garden - September 18, 1988](https://www.dead.net/show/september-18-1988) [29]
